items.title: In 1999, He Put $1,700 Worth of His Company’s Stock Into a Roth IRA. By 2019, Peter Thiel Had $5 Billion in Retirement Assets That Will Never Be Taxed Again. Here’s the Roth Conversion Math for a 58-Year-Old With $400,000 in a 401(k)
items.summary: Peter Thiel bought 1.7 million PayPal shares for about $1,700 inside a Roth IRA in 1999; by the end of 2019 the account held $5 billion, ProPublica found, and none of it will be taxed on the way out. A 58-year-old with $400,000 in a 401(k) can buy the same account at a known price: $66,500 a year at the 12% bracket costs $5,800 and clears the account by 65 for $40,600 in all, against a $41,307 RMD at 75 taxed at 22% that pulls 72% of his Social Security into taxable income.
